questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study far away from Denmark and experience a completely different part of the world. Asia felt exciting because it offered new cultures, opportunities to travel, and many countries nearby to explore. Singapore was especially attractive because English is the main language, which makes studying and daily life much easier. In addition, NUS has a very strong academic reputation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We got a lot of information from the university and it could be quite hard getting an overview because there was so much but generally we got all the info we needed in good time and there was many easy ways to access it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any but it was possible to get a buddy from the university if you apply for it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was pretty straight forward.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of campus housing options which can be overwhelming but you can apply for rooms with aircon / no aircon and different places depending on how social you want to be where you live.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived at the PGP residence. We have 1 kitchen for approximately 15 people to use. Was almost never in use because the food on campus is cheap and you need to get your own kitchen accessories.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I would recommended it. At PGP (and the different houses which was right next to it) there is a lot of other exchangers which makes it easier to meet new people. But it seemed like all the places was very nice.
It is very warm in Singapore so getting an aircondition is very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration starts early but it is a very reasonable system. You prioritise your top-10 classes and the you can see which classes you got. There are multiple rounds so it is possible to get into a class even though you did not get in the class in round 1.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of info online and the answer quickly if you send and email to NUS.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite succesfull and got the classes I wanted pretty much.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Remember there is multiple round to get the courses. 
You have to sign up for which tutorial you want to go to in each course in the beginning of the stay. Use NUSmods to check for times and schedule.
They give a lot of information out and if you check your mail everyday you probably won't miss anything.
Also use NUSmods to see info on different courses such as: Reviews, prerequisites, schedule etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is more or less same level as in University of Copehagen

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is a different style of learning on NUS. You have tutorials (which reminds a bit of "øvelsestimer"), which are usually 1 hour where you have to prepare and present solutions to questions in front of the class. It is mandatory to show up to these.
Some of the exams (not all) you have to remember more than understanding the formulas because you have to be very fast in the exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EC3333 Financial Economics
EC3343 International Finance
GEX1010 Thinking Like An Economist
GESS1005 South Asia In Singapore

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
EC3333 Financial Economics and EC3343 International Finance:
For Econ students these courses are a good introduction to finance I think. You learn a lot of basic stuff.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were some extra fees such as mandatory insurance, MSF etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: You can eat very cheap if you want to. Economically, it does not make sense to cook your own food since the supermarkets are quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of sports and you have many opportunities and time to try it out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of events and sports club. Show up to the events, sports club etc.
It is very fun and you get to meet a lot of new people. Both exchangers and locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I will recommend to go travel with friends you meet in Singapore. People are very nice and open to travel. Remember to get it done because time flies on exchange :))
Malaysia and Indonesia are super close and you can do tons of nice things there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
There is definitely a culture shock with the food, social interactions, weather etc.
But I would say because everybody talks English it makes much easier to adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not socialise that much with the local student and they can be a bit shy. But I'm sure if you are very interested in talking and socialising with local students they are very nice and polite.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To get use to the food and the weather (with no seasons as we know from Denmark) was a bit challenging. But generally people are very nice and open to every culture which makes it easier to adapt.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Kind of also the same. The food was super good and you can find some very nice places very cheap if you go out to eat in the Hawker centres (Big recommendation).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go out to travel with new people. It is super fun and very convenient from Singapore
2. Try a 1000-1999 course not from your area of study. It is a good opportunity to learn something new and everyone can join those courses.
3. Explore the city and go often out to eat in different hawker centres. It is super fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep yourself updated on the mail through the whole semester. You get a lot of information which is important and a lot of information which is not important at all. Make sure to check your mail everyday not to miss deadlines.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding for me was both to experience a school like NUS but also to meet new people and have some good experiences with them as well.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think to find the balance between school, travel and socialising. Because you have to a lor of hours to study and they way of studying here is a bit different from Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
